title: Israeli navy intercepts convoy of aid ships bound for Gaza | Myrtle Beach Sun News
text:
The Global Sumud Flotilla docks at the port of Bizerte, in northern Tunisia. The flotilla, which aims to break Israel's blockade on Gaza, has postponed its departure to Saturday due to logistical reasons, according to organizers. (Hasan Mrad/Zuma Press/dpa/TNS) Hasan Mrad TNS TEL AVIV - The Israeli navy has intercepted a flotilla of ships carrying activists and humanitarian supplies bound for the Gaza Strip.
"Global Sumud Flotilla intercepted by Israeli naval forces," the group said in a brief statement late Wednesday on its Telegram channel.
The Israeli Foreign Ministry said in a statement on X that several vessels had been safely stopped and that their passengers were being transferred to an Israeli port.
Earlier, activists posted on social media that soldiers had boarded some of the vessels, while livestreamed footage showed others in life jackets apparently awaiting Israeli forces to do so.
The flotilla of more than 40 motorboats and sailing vessels had come within 70 to 80 nautical miles of Gaza when the Israeli operations began, activists said.
Participants, including Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg, say they aim to deliver humanitarian aid to war-ravaged Gaza and protest Israel's military campaign in the sealed-off territory.
"Greta and her friends are safe and healthy," the Israeli Foreign Ministry said on X late Wednesday.
Turkish government condemns Israeli operation The Turkish government strongly condemned the Israeli military operation.
"The attack carried out by Israeli forces in international waters against the Global Sumud Flotilla, which set sail to deliver humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza, constitutes an act of terrorism that gravely violates international law and endangers the lives of innocent civilians," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"We hope that this attack will not undermine ongoing efforts to secure a ceasefire in Gaza," the ministry added.
Protests in Rome and Berlin Protests broke out in Italy late on Wednesday following Israel's interception. In Rome, dozens of demonstrators gathered outside the city's main train station in the evening. Authorities temporarily closed access to the station and shut down the nearby metro station as a precaution.
According to the newspaper La Repubblica, a group of protesters marched towards the office of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, accusing her right-wing government of failing to show solidarity with the flotilla activists. Some chanted the government had "blood on its hands."
Protests also took place in Berlin, where around 300 people rallied against the flotilla's interception. At a rally in front of the central station, police said some demonstrators threw bottles at officers and chanted banned slogans. Several people were detained, police said.
Israel: Flotilla 'not interested in aid, but in provocation' The Global Sumud Flotilla set sail from Barcelona in late August. "Sumud" means steadfastness in Arabic.
Offers to deliver the flotilla's aid supplies to Gaza via an Israeli port have been rejected by the activists, who want to distribute the aid themselves.
Flotilla spokesman Thiago Ávila said the group refused the Israeli offer because humanitarian aid should not be handed to "the occupying power" in Gaza.
Palestinians, he said, had the right to control their own borders.
The Israeli government has made it clear that it will prevent this attempt, as it has with all previous efforts to break the blockade of Gaza. The government refers to the flotilla as a Hamas operation.
"The sole purpose of the Hamas-Sumud flotilla is provocation," the Israeli Foreign Ministry said on X.
"Israel, Italy, Greece, and the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem have all offered and continue to offer the flotilla a way to peacefully deliver any aid they might have to Gaza. The flotilla refused because they are not interested in aid, but in provocation."
"The Israeli Navy has reached out to the Hamas-Sumud flotilla and asked them to change course. Israel has informed the flotilla that it is approaching an active combat zone and violating a lawful naval blockade. Israel reiterated the offer to transfer any aid peacefully through safe channels to Gaza."
